<details><summary>Tool use: **run_terminal_cmd** • Run command: cd "C:\Users\downl\Desktop\codex-main"; $py = @'
import os
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path('.').resolve()
TARGET_DIRS = [ROOT / 'codex-rs', ROOT / 'sdk' / 'typescript']
SKIP_DIR_NAMES = {'.git', 'target', 'node_modules', '.venv', '__pycache__'}

class ConflictError(Exception):
    pass

def resolve_keep_head(text: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    out: list[str] = []
    i = 0
    resolved = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        if line.startswith('<<<<<<< '):
            resolved += 1
            i += 1
            head: list[str] = []
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].startswith('======='):
                head.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            if i >= len(lines):
                raise ConflictError('missing =======')
            i += 1  # skip =======
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].startswith('>>>>>>> '):
                i += 1
            if i >= len(lines):
                raise ConflictError('missing >>>>>>>')
            i += 1  # skip >>>>>>>
            out.extend(head)
            continue
        out.append(line)
        i += 1
    return ''.join(out), resolved

def iter_files(base: Path):
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(base):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in SKIP_DIR_NAMES]
        for name in files:
            p = Path(root) / name
            yield p

changed: list[tuple[Path, int]] = []
errors: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []

for base in TARGET_DIRS:
    if not base.exists():
        continue
    for p in iter_files(base):
        try:
            data = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            # Skip binary/unknown encodings safely.
            continue
        if '<<<<<<< ' not in data:
            continue
        try:
            new_data, count = resolve_keep_head(data)
        except ConflictError as e:
            errors.append((p, str(e)))
            continue
        if count and new_data != data:
            p.write_text(new_data, encoding='utf-8', newline='')
            changed.append((p, count))

print(f"resolved_files={len(changed)}")
print(f"errors={len(errors)}")
for p, n in changed[:50]:
    rel = p.relative_to(ROOT)
    print(f"{rel} : blocks={n}")
if len(changed) > 50:
    print(f"... and {len(changed) - 50} more")

if errors:
    print('--- errors ---')
    for p, msg in errors[:50]:
        rel = p.relative_to(ROOT)
        print(f"{rel} : {msg}")
    raise SystemExit(1)
'@; py -3 -c $py</summary>

import os
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
TARGET_DIRS = [ROOT / 'docs', ROOT / 'codex-cli', ROOT / 'scripts']
TARGET_FILES = [ROOT / 'LICENSE']
SKIP_DIR_NAMES = {'.git', '_docs', '.specstory', 'target', 'node_modules', '.venv', '__pycache__'}

class ConflictError(Exception):
    pass

def resolve_keep_head(text: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    out: list[str] = []
    i = 0
    resolved = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        if line.startswith('<<<<<<< '):
            resolved += 1
            i += 1
            head: list[str] = []
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].startswith('======='):
                head.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            if i >= len(lines):
                raise ConflictError('missing =======')
            i += 1  # skip =======
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].startswith('>>>>>>> '):
                i += 1
            if i >= len(lines):
                raise ConflictError('missing >>>>>>>')
            i += 1  # skip >>>>>>>
            out.extend(head)
            continue
        out.append(line)
        i += 1
    return ''.join(out), resolved

def iter_files(base: Path):
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(base):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in SKIP_DIR_NAMES]
        for name in files:
            yield Path(root) / name

changed: list[tuple[Path, int]] = []
errors: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []

for p in TARGET_FILES:

    if '<<<<<<< ' not in data:

    try:

        errors.append((p, str(e)))
        continue
    if count and new_data != data:
        p.write_text(new_data, encoding='utf-8', newline='')
        changed.append((p, count))

for base in TARGET_DIRS:

 dry_run: bool,\r\n        executed: &amp;mut usize,\r\n        successful: &amp;mut usize,\r\n        failed: &amp;mut usize,\r\n        errors: &amp;mut Vec&lt;String&gt;,\r\n        rollback:    } else if total_risk_score &gt;= 1.5 {\r\n            RiskLevel::High\r\n        } else if total_risk_score &gt;= 1.0 {\r\n            RiskLevel::Medium\r\n        } else if total_risk_score &gt;= ) -&gt; Result&lt;Vec&lt;ImprovementAction&gt;, String&gt; {\r\n        let mut actions = Vec::new();\r\n\r\n        for improvement in improvements {\r\n            // Filter by risk tolerance\r\n }\r\n\r\n        score.min(1.0)\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    fn assess_improvement_risk(&amp;self, improvement: &amp;PotentialImprovement) -&gt; RiskLevel {\r\n        match improvement.improvement_type {\r\n risk_score &gt;= 1.0 {\r\n            RiskLevel::High\r\n        } else if risk_score &gt;= 0.7 {\r\n            RiskLevel::Medium\r\n        } else if risk_score &gt;= 0.3 {\r\n            RiskLevel::Low\r\n        } else {\r\n            RiskLevel::VeryLow\r\n        };\r\n\r\n        let risk_mitigation_strategies = match overall_risk_level {\r\n            RiskLevel::VeryHigh =&gt; ],\r\n            RiskLevel::Medium =&gt; vec![\r\n                \"Ensure test coverage for modified code\".to_string(),\r\n                \"Plan for quick rollback if issues std::io::Result&lt;Self&gt; {\n        let codex_home = find_codex_home()?;\n\n        let root_value = load_resolved_config(\n            &amp;codex_home,\n            cli_overrides,\n            crate::config_loader::LoaderOverrides::default(),\n        )\n        .await?;\n\n        let cfg = deserialize_config_toml_with_base(root_value, &amp;codex_home).map_err(|e| {\n            tracing::error!(\"Failed to deserialize overridden config: {e}\");\n            e\n        })?;\n\n        Self::load_from_base_config_with_overrides(cfg, overrides, codex_home)\n    }\n}\n\npub async fn load_config_as_toml_with_cli_overrides(\n    codex_home: &amp;Path,\n    cli_overrides: Vec&lt;(String, TomlValue)&gt;,\n) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;ConfigToml&gt; {\n    let root_value = load_resolved_config(\n        codex_home,\n        cli_overrides,\n        crate::config_loader::LoaderOverrides::default(),\n    )\n    .await?;\n\n    let cfg = deserialize_config_toml_with_base(root_value, codex_home).map_err(|e| {\n        tracing::error!(\"Failed to deserialize overridden config: {e}\");\n        e\n    })?;\n\n    Ok(cfg)\n}\n\nasync fn load_resolved_config(\n    codex_home: &amp;Path,\n    cli_overrides: Vec&lt;(String, TomlValue)&gt;,\n    overrides: crate::config_loader::LoaderOverrides,\n) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;TomlValue&gt; {\n    let layers = load_config_layers_with_overrides(codex_home, overrides).await?;\n    Ok(apply_overlays(layers, cli_overrides))\n}\n\nfn apply_overlays(\n    layers: LoadedConfigLayers,\n    cli_overrides: Vec&lt;(String, TomlValue)&gt;,\n) -&gt; TomlValue {\n    let LoadedConfigLayers {\n        mut base,\n        managed_config,\n        managed_preferences,\n    } = layers;\n\n    for (path, value) in cli_overrides.into_iter() {\n        apply_toml_override(&amp;mut base, &amp;path, value);\n    }\n\n    for overlay in [managed_config, managed_preferences].into_iter().flatten() {\n        merge_toml_values(&amp;mut base, &amp;overlay);\n    }\n\n    base\n}\n\nfn deserialize_config_toml_with_base(\n    root_value: TomlValue,\n    config_base_dir: &amp;Path,\n) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;ConfigToml&gt; {\n    // This guard ensures that any relative paths that is deserialized into an\n    // [AbsolutePathBuf] is resolved against &#96;config_base_dir&#96;.\n    let _guard = AbsolutePathBufGuard::new(config_base_dir);\n    root_value\n        .try_into()\n        .map_err(|e| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, e))\n}\n\npub async fn load_global_mcp_servers(\n    codex_home: &amp;Path,\n) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;BTreeMap&lt;String, McpServerConfig&gt;&gt; {\n    let root_value = load_config_as_toml(codex_home).await?;\n    let Some(servers_value) = root_value.get(\"mcp_servers\") else {\n        return Ok(BTreeMap::new());\n    };\n\n    ensure_no_inline_bearer_tokens(servers_value)?;\n\n    servers_value\n        .clone()\n        .try_into()\n        .map_err(|e| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, e))\n}\n\n/// We briefly allowed plain text bearer_token fields in MCP server configs.\n/// We want to warn people who recently added these fields but can remove this after a few months.\nfn ensure_no_inline_bearer_tokens(value: &amp;TomlValue) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;()&gt; {\n    let Some(servers_table) = value.as_table() else {\n        return Ok(());\n    };\n\n    for (server_name, server_value) in servers_table {\n        if let Some(server_table) = server_value.as_table()\n            &amp;&amp; server_table.contains_key(\"bearer_token\")\n        {\n            let message = format!(\n                \"mcp_servers.{server_name} uses unsupported &#96;bearer_token&#96;; set &#96;bearer_token_env_var&#96;.\"\n            );\n            return Err(std::io::Error::new(ErrorKind::InvalidData, message));\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\npub(crate) fn set_project_trusted_inner(\n    doc: &amp;mut DocumentMut,\n    project_path: &amp;Path,\n) -&gt; anyhow::Result&lt;()&gt; {\n    // Ensure we render a human-friendly structure:\n    //\n    // [projects]\n    // [projects.\"/path/to/project\"]\n    // trust_level = \"trusted\"\n    //\n    // rather than inline tables like:\n    //\n    // [projects]\n    // \"/path/to/project\" = { trust_level = \"trusted\" }\n    let project_key = project_path.to_string_lossy().to_string();\n\n    // Ensure top-level &#96;projects&#96; exists as a non-inline, explicit table. If it\n    // exists but was previously represented as a non-table (e.g., inline),\n    // replace it with an explicit table.\n    {\n        let root = doc.as_table_mut();\n        // If &#96;projects&#96; exists but isn't a standard table (e.g., it's an inline table),\n        // convert it to an explicit table while preserving existing entries.\n        let existing_projects = root.get(\"projects\").cloned();\n        if existing_projects.as_ref().is_none_or(|i| !i.is_table()) {\n            let mut projects_tbl = toml_edit::Table::new();\n            projects_tbl.set_implicit(true);\n\n            // If there was an existing inline table, migrate its entries to explicit tables.\n            if let Some(inline_tbl) = existing_projects.as_ref().and_then(|i| i.as_inline_table()) {\n                for (k, v) in inline_tbl.iter() {\n                    if let Some(inner_tbl) = v.as_inline_table() {\n                        let new_tbl = inner_tbl.clone().into_table();\n                        projects_tbl.insert(k, toml_edit::Item::Table(new_tbl));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            root.insert(\"projects\", toml_edit::Item::Table(projects_tbl));\n        }\n    }\n    let Some(projects_tbl) = doc[\"projects\"].as_table_mut() else {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n            \"projects table missing after initialization\"\n        ));\n    };\n\n    // Ensure the per-project entry is its own explicit table. If it exists but\n    // is not a table (e.g., an inline table), replace it with an explicit table.\n    let needs_proj_table = !projects_tbl.contains_key(project_key.as_str())\n        || projects_tbl\n            .get(project_key.as_str())\n            .and_then(|i| i.as_table())\n            .is_none();\n    if needs_proj_table {\n        projects_tbl.insert(project_key.as_str(), toml_edit::table());\n    }\n    let Some(proj_tbl) = projects_tbl\n        .get_mut(project_key.as_str())\n        .and_then(|i| i.as_table_mut())\n    else {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"project table missing for {project_key}\"));\n    };\n    proj_tbl.set_implicit(false);\n    proj_tbl[\"trust_level\"] = toml_edit::value(\"trusted\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Patch &#96;CODEX_HOME/config.toml&#96; project state.\n/// Use with caution.\npub fn set_project_trusted(codex_home: &amp;Path, project_path: &amp;Path) -&gt; anyhow::Result&lt;()&gt; {\n    use crate::config::edit::ConfigEditsBuilder;\n\n    ConfigEditsBuilder::new(codex_home)\n        .set_project_trusted(project_path)\n        .apply_blocking()\n}\n\n/// Apply a single dotted-path override onto a TOML value.\nfn apply_toml_override(root: &amp;mut TomlValue, path: &amp;str, value: TomlValue) {\n    use toml::value::Table;\n\n    let segments: Vec&lt;&amp;str&gt; = path.split('.').collect();\n    let mut current = root;\n\n    for (idx, segment) in segments.iter().enumerate() {\n        let is_last = idx == segments.len() - 1;\n\n        if is_last {\n            match current {\n                TomlValue::Table(table) =&gt; {\n                    table.insert(segment.to_string(), value);\n                }\n                _ =&gt; {\n                    let mut table = Table::new();\n                    table.insert(segment.to_string(), value);\n                    *current = TomlValue::Table(table);\n                }\n            }\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // Traverse or create intermediate object.\n        match current {\n            TomlValue::Table(table) =&gt; {\n                current = table\n                    .entry(segment.to_string())\n                    .or_insert_with(|| TomlValue::Table(Table::new()));\n            }\n            _ =&gt; {\n                *current = TomlValue::Table(Table::new());\n                if let TomlValue::Table(tbl) = current {\n                    current = tbl\n                        .entry(segment.to_string())\n                        .or_insert_with(|| TomlValue::Table(Table::new()));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Base config deserialized from ~/.codex/config.toml.\n#[derive(Deserialize, Debug, Clone, Default, for UserSavedConfig {\n    fn from(config_toml: ConfigToml) -&gt; Self {\n        let profiles = config_toml\n            .profiles\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|(k, v)| (k, v.into()))\n            .collect();\n\n        Self {\n            approval_policy: config_toml.approval_policy,\n            sandbox_mode: config_toml.sandbox_mode,\n            sandbox_settings: config_toml.sandbox_workspace_write.map(From::from),\n            forced_chatgpt_workspace_id: config_toml.forced_chatgpt_workspace_id,\n            forced_login_method: config_toml.forced_login_method,\n            model: config_toml.model,\n            model_reasoning_effort: config_toml.model_reasoning_effort,\n            model_reasoning_summary: config_toml.model_reasoning_summary,\n            model_verbosity: config_toml.model_verbosity,\n            tools: config_toml.tools.map(From::from),\n            profile: config_toml.profile,\n            profiles,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Deserialize, Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ProjectConfig {\n    pub trust_level: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n}\n\nimpl ProjectConfig {\n    pub fn is_trusted(&amp;self) -&gt; SandboxPolicyResolution {\n        let resolved_sandbox_mode = sandbox_mode_override\n            .or(profile_sandbox_mode)\n            .or(self.sandbox_mode)\n            .or_else(|| {\n                // if no sandbox_mode is set, but user has marked directory as trusted, use WorkspaceWrite\n                self.get_active_project(resolved_cwd).and_then(|p| {\n                    if p.is_trusted() {\n                        Some(SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite)\n                    } else {\n                        None\n                    }\n                })\n            })\n            .unwrap_or(SandboxMode::DangerFullAccess); // YOLO mode: default to full access\n        let mut sandbox_policy = match resolved_sandbox_mode {\n            SandboxMode::ReadOnly =&gt; SandboxPolicy::new_read_only_policy(),\n            SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite =&gt; match self.sandbox_workspace_write.as_ref() {\n                Some(SandboxWorkspaceWrite {\n                    writable_roots,\n                    network_access,\n                    exclude_tmpdir_env_var,\n                    exclude_slash_tmp,\n                }) =&gt; SandboxPolicy::WorkspaceWrite {\n                    writable_roots: writable_roots.clone(),\n                    network_access: *network_access,\n                    exclude_tmpdir_env_var: *exclude_tmpdir_env_var,\n                    exclude_slash_tmp: *exclude_slash_tmp,\n                },\n                None =&gt; SandboxPolicy::new_workspace_write_policy(),\n            },\n            SandboxMode::DangerFullAccess =&gt; SandboxPolicy::DangerFullAccess,\n        };\n        let mut forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows = false;\n        if cfg!(target_os = \"windows\")\n            &amp;&amp; matches!(resolved_sandbox_mode, SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite)\n            // If the experimental Windows sandbox is enabled, do not force a downgrade.\n            &amp;&amp; crate::safety::get_platform_sandbox().is_none()\n        {\n            sandbox_policy = SandboxPolicy::new_read_only_policy();\n            forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows = true;\n        }\n        SandboxPolicyResolution {\n            policy: sandbox_policy,\n            forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Resolves the cwd to an existing project, or returns None if ConfigToml\n    /// does not contain a project corresponding to cwd or a git repo for cwd\n    pub fn get_active_project(&amp;self, resolved_cwd: &amp;Path) -&gt; Option&lt;ProjectConfig&gt; {\n        let projects = self.projects.clone().unwrap_or_default();\n\n        if let Some(project_config) = projects.get(&amp;resolved_cwd.to_string_lossy().to_string()) {\n            return Some(project_config.clone());\n        }\n\n        // If cwd lives inside a git repo/worktree, check whether the root git project\n        // (the primary repository working directory) is trusted. This lets\n        // worktrees inherit trust from the main project.\n        if let Some(repo_root) = resolve_root_git_project_for_trust(resolved_cwd)\n            &amp;&amp; let Some(project_config_for_root) =\n                projects.get(&amp;repo_root.to_string_lossy().to_string_lossy().to_string())\n        {\n            return Some(project_config_for_root.clone());\n        }\n\n        None\n    }\n\n    pub fn get_config_profile(\n        &amp;self,\n        override_profile: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n    ) -&gt; Result&lt;ConfigProfile, std::io::Error&gt; {\n        let profile = override_profile.or_else(|| self.profile.clone());\n\n        match profile {\n            Some(key) =&gt; {\n                if let Some(profile) = self.profiles.get(key.as_str()) {\n profile &#96;{key}&#96; not found\"),\n                ))\n            }\n            None =&gt; Ok(ConfigProfile::default()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Optional overrides for user configuration std::io::Result&lt;ConfigToml&gt; {\n    // This guard ensures that any relative paths that is deserialized into an\n    // [AbsolutePathBuf] is resolved against &#96;config_base_dir&#96;.\n    let _guard = AbsolutePathBufGuard::new(config_base_dir);\n    root_value\n        .try_into()\n        .map_err(|e| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, e))\n}\n\npub async fn load_global_mcp_servers(\n    codex_home: &amp;Path,\n) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;BTreeMap&lt;String, McpServerConfig&gt;&gt; {\n    let root_value = load_config_as_toml(codex_home).await?;\n    let Some(servers_value) = root_value.get(\"mcp_servers\") else {\n        return Ok(BTreeMap::new());\n    };\n\n    ensure_no_inline_bearer_tokens(servers_value)?;\n\n    servers_value\n        .clone()\n        .try_into()\n        .map_err(|e| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, e))\n}\n\n/// We briefly allowed plain text bearer_token fields in MCP server configs.\n/// We want to warn people who recently added these fields but can remove this after a few months.\nfn ensure_no_inline_bearer_tokens(value: &amp;TomlValue) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;()&gt; {\n    let Some(servers_table) = value.as_table() else {\n        return Ok(());\n    };\n\n    for (server_name, server_value) in servers_table {\n        if let Some(server_table) = server_value.as_table()\n            &amp;&amp; server_table.contains_key(\"bearer_token\")\n        {\n            let message = format!(\n                \"mcp_servers.{server_name} uses unsupported &#96;bearer_token&#96;; set &#96;bearer_token_env_var&#96;.\"\n            );\n            return Err(std::io::Error::new(ErrorKind::InvalidData, message));\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\npub(crate) fn set_project_trusted_inner(\n    doc: &amp;mut DocumentMut,\n    project_path: &amp;Path,\n) -&gt; anyhow::Result&lt;()&gt; {\n    // Ensure we render a human-friendly structure:\n    //\n    // [projects]\n    // [projects.\"/path/to/project\"]\n    // trust_level = \"trusted\"\n    //\n    // rather than inline tables like:\n    //\n    // [projects]\n    // \"/path/to/project\" = { trust_level = \"trusted\" }\n    let project_key = project_path.to_string_lossy().to_string();\n\n    // Ensure top-level &#96;projects&#96; exists as a non-inline, explicit table. If it\n    // exists but was previously represented as a non-table (e.g., inline),\n    // replace it with an explicit table.\n    {\n        let root = doc.as_table_mut();\n        // If &#96;projects&#96; exists but isn't a standard table (e.g., it's an inline table),\n        // convert it to an explicit table while preserving existing entries.\n        let existing_projects = root.get(\"projects\").cloned();\n        if existing_projects.as_ref().is_none_or(|i| !i.is_table()) {\n            let mut projects_tbl = toml_edit::Table::new();\n            projects_tbl.set_implicit(true);\n\n            // If there was an existing inline table, migrate its entries to explicit tables.\n            if let Some(inline_tbl) = existing_projects.as_ref().and_then(|i| i.as_inline_table()) {\n                for (k, v) in inline_tbl.iter() {\n                    if let Some(inner_tbl) = v.as_inline_table() {\n                        let new_tbl = inner_tbl.clone().into_table();\n                        projects_tbl.insert(k, toml_edit::Item::Table(new_tbl));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            root.insert(\"projects\", toml_edit::Item::Table(projects_tbl));\n        }\n    }\n    let Some(projects_tbl) = doc[\"projects\"].as_table_mut() else {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n            \"projects table missing after initialization\"\n        ));\n    };\n\n    // Ensure the per-project entry is its own explicit table. If it exists but\n    // is not a table (e.g., an inline table), replace it with an explicit table.\n    let needs_proj_table = !projects_tbl.contains_key(project_key.as_str())\n        || projects_tbl\n            .get(project_key.as_str())\n            .and_then(|i| i.as_table())\n            .is_none();\n    if needs_proj_table {\n        projects_tbl.insert(project_key.as_str(), toml_edit::table());\n    }\n    let Some(proj_tbl) = projects_tbl\n        .get_mut(project_key.as_str())\n        .and_then(|i| i.as_table_mut())\n    else {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"project table missing for {project_key}\"));\n    };\n    proj_tbl.set_implicit(false);\n    proj_tbl[\"trust_level\"] = toml_edit::value(\"trusted\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Patch &#96;CODEX_HOME/config.toml&#96; project state.\n/// Use with caution.\npub fn set_project_trusted(codex_home: &amp;Path, project_path: &amp;Path) -&gt; anyhow::Result&lt;()&gt; {\n    use crate::config::edit::ConfigEditsBuilder;\n\n    ConfigEditsBuilder::new(codex_home)\n        .set_project_trusted(project_path)\n        .apply_blocking()\n}\n\n/// Apply a single dotted-path override onto a TOML value.\nfn apply_toml_override(root: &amp;mut TomlValue, path: &amp;str, value: TomlValue) {\n    use toml::value::Table;\n\n    let segments: Vec&lt;&amp;str&gt; = path.split('.').collect();\n    let mut current = root;\n\n    for (idx, segment) in segments.iter().enumerate() {\n        let is_last = idx == segments.len() - 1;\n\n        if is_last {\n            match current {\n                TomlValue::Table(table) =&gt; {\n                    table.insert(segment.to_string(), value);\n                }\n                _ =&gt; {\n                    let mut table = Table::new();\n                    table.insert(segment.to_string(), value);\n                    *current = TomlValue::Table(table);\n                }\n            }\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // Traverse or create intermediate object.\n        match current {\n            TomlValue::Table(table) =&gt; {\n                current = table\n                    .entry(segment.to_string())\n                    .or_insert_with(|| TomlValue::Table(Table::new()));\n            }\n            _ =&gt; {\n                *current = TomlValue::Table(Table::new());\n                if let TomlValue::Table(tbl) = current {\n                    current = tbl\n                        .entry(segment.to_string())\n                        .or_insert_with(|| TomlValue::Table(Table::new()));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Base config deserialized from ~/.codex/config.toml.\n#[derive(Deserialize, Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]\npub struct ConfigToml {\n    /// Optional override of model selection.\n    pub model: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n    /// Review model override used by the &#96;/review&#96; feature.\n    pub review_model: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// Provider to use from the model_providers map.\n    pub model_provider: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// Size of the context window for the model, in tokens.\n    pub model_context_window: Option&lt;i64&gt;,\n\n    /// Maximum number of output tokens.\n    pub model_max_output_tokens: Option&lt;i64&gt;,\n\n    /// Token usage threshold triggering auto-compaction of conversation history.\n    pub model_auto_compact_token_limit: Option&lt;i64&gt;,\n\n    /// Default approval policy for executing commands.\n    pub approval_policy: Optional external command to spawn for end-user notifications.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub notify: Option&lt;Vec&lt;String&gt;&gt;,\n\n    /// System instructions.\n    pub instructions: keyring service.\n    /// auto: Use the keyring if available, otherwise use a file.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub cli_auth_credentials_store: Option&lt;AuthCredentialsStoreMode&gt;,\n\n    /// the Codex home directory.\n    /// auto (default): Use the OS-specific keyring service if available, otherwise use a file.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub mcp_oauth_credentials_store: for UserSavedConfig {\n    fn from(config_toml: ConfigToml) -&gt; Self {\n        let profiles = config_toml\n            .profiles\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|(k, v)| (k, v.into()))\n            .collect();\n\n        Self {\n            approval_policy: config_toml.approval_policy,\n            sandbox_mode: config_toml.sandbox_mode,\n            sandbox_settings: config_toml.sandbox_workspace_write.map(From::from),\n            forced_chatgpt_workspace_id: config_toml.forced_chatgpt_workspace_id,\n            forced_login_method: config_toml.forced_login_method,\n            model: config_toml.model,\n            model_reasoning_effort: config_toml.model_reasoning_effort,\n            model_reasoning_summary: config_toml.model_reasoning_summary,\n            model_verbosity: config_toml.model_verbosity,\n            tools: config_toml.tools.map(From::from),\n            profile: config_toml.profile,\n            profiles,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Deserialize, Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ProjectConfig {\n    pub trust_level: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n}\n\nimpl ProjectConfig {\n    pub fn is_trusted(&amp;self) -&gt; SandboxPolicyResolution {\n        let resolved_sandbox_mode = sandbox_mode_override\n            .or(profile_sandbox_mode)\n            .or(self.sandbox_mode)\n            .or_else(|| {\n                // if no sandbox_mode is set, but user has marked directory as trusted, use WorkspaceWrite\n                self.get_active_project(resolved_cwd).and_then(|p| {\n                    if p.is_trusted() {\n                        Some(SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite)\n                    } else {\n                        None\n                    }\n                })\n            })\n            .unwrap_or(SandboxMode::DangerFullAccess); // YOLO mode: default to full access\n        let mut sandbox_policy = match resolved_sandbox_mode {\n            SandboxMode::ReadOnly =&gt; SandboxPolicy::new_read_only_policy(),\n            SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite =&gt; match self.sandbox_workspace_write.as_ref() {\n                Some(SandboxWorkspaceWrite {\n                    writable_roots,\n                    network_access,\n                    exclude_tmpdir_env_var,\n                    exclude_slash_tmp,\n                }) =&gt; SandboxPolicy::WorkspaceWrite {\n                    writable_roots: writable_roots.clone(),\n                    network_access: *network_access,\n                    exclude_tmpdir_env_var: *exclude_tmpdir_env_var,\n                    exclude_slash_tmp: *exclude_slash_tmp,\n                },\n                None =&gt; SandboxPolicy::new_workspace_write_policy(),\n            },\n            SandboxMode::DangerFullAccess =&gt; SandboxPolicy::DangerFullAccess,\n        };\n        let mut forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows = false;\n        if cfg!(target_os = \"windows\")\n            &amp;&amp; matches!(resolved_sandbox_mode, SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite)\n            // If the experimental Windows sandbox is enabled, do not force a downgrade.\n            &amp;&amp; crate::safety::get_platform_sandbox().is_none()\n        {\n            sandbox_policy = SandboxPolicy::new_read_only_policy();\n            forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows = true;\n        }\n        SandboxPolicyResolution {\n            policy: sandbox_policy,\n            forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Resolves the cwd to an existing project, or returns None if ConfigToml\n    /// does not contain a project corresponding to cwd or a git repo for cwd\n    pub fn get_active_project(&amp;self, resolved_cwd: &amp;Path) -&gt; Option&lt;ProjectConfig&gt; {\n        let projects = self.projects.clone().unwrap_or_default();\n\n        if let Some(project_config) = projects.get(&amp;resolved_cwd.to_string_lossy().to_string()) {\n            return Some(project_config.clone());\n        }\n\n        // If cwd lives inside a git repo/worktree, check whether the root git project\n        // (the primary repository working directory) is trusted. This lets\n        // worktrees inherit trust from the main project.\n        if let Some(repo_root) = resolve_root_git_project_for_trust(resolved_cwd)\n            &amp;&amp; let Some(project_config_for_root) =\n                projects.get(&amp;repo_root.to_string_lossy().to_string_lossy().to_string())\n        {\n            return Some(project_config_for_root.clone());\n        }\n\n        None\n    }\n\n    pub fn get_config_profile(\n        &amp;self,\n        override_profile: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n    ) -&gt; Result&lt;ConfigProfile, std::io::Error&gt; {\n        let profile = override_profile.or_else(|| self.profile.clone());\n\n        match profile {\n            Some(key) =&gt; {\n                if let Some(profile) = self.profiles.get(key.as_str()) {\n std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound,\n                        format!(\"config profile &#96;{key}&#96; not found\"),\n                    )\n                })?\n                .clone(),\n            None web_search_request: override_tools_web_search_request,\n        };\n\n        let features = Features::from_config(&amp;cfg, &amp;config_profile, feature_overrides);\n        #[cfg(target_os = \"windows\")]\n        {\n            crate::safety::set_windows_sandbox_enabled(features.enabled(Feature::WindowsSandbox));\n        }\n\n        let resolved_cwd = {\n            use std::env;\n\n            match cwd {\n                None =&gt; {\n                    tracing::info!(\"cwd not set, using current dir\");\n                    env::current_dir()?\n                }\n                Some(p) if p.is_absolute() =&gt; p,\n                Some(p) =&gt; {\n                    // Resolve relative path against the current working directory.\n                    tracing::info!(\"cwd is relative, resolving against current dir\");\n                    let mut current = env::current_dir()?;\n                    current.push(p);\n                    current\n                }\n writable_roots, .. } = &amp;mut sandbox_policy {\n            for path in additional_writable_roots {\n                if !writable_roots.iter().any(|existing| existing == &amp;path) {\n projects_tbl\n            .get(project_key.as_str())\n            .and_then(|i| i.as_table())\n            .is_none();\n    if needs_proj_table {\n        projects_tbl.insert(project_key.as_str(), toml_edit::table());\n    }\n    let Some(proj_tbl) = projects_tbl\n        .get_mut(project_key.as_str())\n        .and_then(|i| i.as_table_mut())\n    else {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"project table missing for {project_key}\"));\n    };\n    proj_tbl.set_implicit(false);\n    proj_tbl[\"trust_level\"] = toml_edit::value(\"trusted\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// onto a TOML value.\nfn apply_toml_override(root: &amp;mut TomlValue, path: &amp;str, value: TomlValue) {\n    use toml::value::Table;\n\n    let segments: Vec&lt;&amp;str&gt; = path.split('.').collect();\n    let mut current = root;\n\n    for (idx, segment) in segments.iter().enumerate() {\n        let is_last = idx == segments.len() - 1;\n\n        if is_last {\n            match current {\n                TomlValue::Table(table) =&gt; {\n                    table.insert(segment.to_string(), value);\n                }\n                _ =&gt; {\n                    let mut table = Table::new();\n                    table.insert(segment.to_string(), value);\n                    *current = TomlValue::Table(table);\n                }\n            }\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // Traverse or create intermediate object.\n        match current {\n            TomlValue::Table(table) =&gt; {\n                current = table\n                    .entry(segment.to_string())\n                    .or_insert_with(|| TomlValue::Table(Table::new()));\n            }\n            _ =&gt; {\n                *current = TomlValue::Table(Table::new());\n                if let TomlValue::Table(tbl) = current {\n                    current = tbl\n                        .entry(segment.to_string())\n                        .or_insert_with(|| TomlValue::Table(Table::new()));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Base config deserialized from ~/.codex/config.toml.\n#[derive(Deserialize, Debug, Clone, Default, // YOLO mode: default to full access\n        let mut sandbox_policy = match resolved_sandbox_mode {\n            SandboxMode::ReadOnly =&gt; SandboxPolicy::new_read_only_policy(),\n            SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite =&gt; match self.sandbox_workspace_write.as_ref() {\n                Some(SandboxWorkspaceWrite {\n                    writable_roots,\n                    network_access,\n                    exclude_tmpdir_env_var,\n                    exclude_slash_tmp,\n                }) =&gt; SandboxPolicy::WorkspaceWrite {\n                    writable_roots: writable_roots.clone(),\n                    network_access: *network_access,\n                    exclude_tmpdir_env_var: *exclude_tmpdir_env_var,\n                    exclude_slash_tmp: *exclude_slash_tmp,\n                },\n                None =&gt; SandboxPolicy::new_workspace_write_policy(),\n            },\n            SandboxMode::DangerFullAccess =&gt; SandboxPolicy::DangerFullAccess,\n        };\n        let mut forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows = false;\n        if cfg!(target_os = \"windows\")\n            &amp;&amp; SandboxPolicy::WorkspaceWrite {\n                    writable_roots: writable_roots.clone(),\n                    network_access: *network_access,\n                    exclude_tmpdir_env_var: *exclude_tmpdir_env_var,\n                    exclude_slash_tmp: *exclude_slash_tmp,\n                },\n                None =&gt; match self.sandbox_workspace_write.as_ref() {\n                Some(SandboxWorkspaceWrite {\n                    writable_roots,\n                    network_access,\n                    exclude_tmpdir_env_var,\n                    exclude_slash_tmp,\n                }) =&gt; SandboxPolicy::WorkspaceWrite {\n                    writable_roots: writable_roots.clone(),\n                    network_access: *network_access,\n                    exclude_tmpdir_env_var: *exclude_tmpdir_env_var,\n                    exclude_slash_tmp: *exclude_slash_tmp,\n                },\n                None =&gt; matches!(resolved_sandbox_mode, SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite)\n            // If the experimental Windows sandbox is enabled, do not force a downgrade.\n            &amp;&amp; crate::safety::get_platform_sandbox().is_none()\n        {\n            sandbox_policy = SandboxPolicy::new_read_only_policy();\n            forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows = true;\n        }\n        SandboxPolicyResolution {\n            policy: sandbox_policy,\n            forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Resolves the cwd to an existing project, or returns None if ConfigToml\n    /// does not contain a project corresponding to cwd or a git repo for cwd\n    pub fn get_active_project(&amp;self, resolved_cwd: &amp;Path) -&gt; This can reduce visual noise when\n    /// users are only interested in the final agent responses.\n    pub hide_agent_reasoning: bool,\n\n    /// When set to &#96;true&#96;, &#96;AgentReasoningRawContentEvent&#96; events will be shown in the UI/output.\n    /// Defaults to &#96;false&#96;.\n    pub show_raw_agent_reasoning: bool,\n\n    /// User-provided instructions from AGENTS.md.\n    pub user_instructions: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// Base instructions override.\n    pub base_instructions: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// Developer instructions override injected as a separate message.\n    pub developer_instructions: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// Compact prompt override.\n    pub compact_prompt: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// Optional external notifier command. If set, citations to files in the model\n    /// output will be hyperlinked using the specified URI scheme.\n    pub file_opener: UriBasedFileOpener,\n\n    /// Path to the &#96;codex-linux-sandbox&#96; executable. This must be set if\n    /// [&#96;crate::exec::SandboxType::LinuxSeccomp&#96;] is used. Note that this\n    /// cannot be set in the config file: it must be set in code via\n    /// [&#96;ConfigOverrides&#96;].\n    ///\n    /// When this program is invoked, arg0 will be set to &#96;codex-linux-sandbox&#96;.\n    pub codex_linux_sandbox_exe: Option&lt;PathBuf&gt;,\n\n    /// Value to use for &#96;reasoning.effort&#96; when making a request using the\n    /// Responses API.\n    pub model_reasoning_effort: Option&lt;ReasoningEffort&gt;,\n\n    /// If not \"none\", the value to use for &#96;reasoning.summary&#96; when making a\n    /// request using the Responses API.\n    pub model_reasoning_summary: ReasoningSummary,\n\n    /// Optional verbosity control for GPT-5 models (Responses API &#96;text.verbosity&#96;).\n    pub model_verbosity: Option&lt;Verbosity&gt;,\n\n    /// Base URL for requests to ChatGPT (as opposed to the OpenAI API).\n    pub chatgpt_base_url: String,\n\n    /// When set, restricts ChatGPT login to a specific workspace identifier.\n    pub forced_chatgpt_workspace_id: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// When set, restricts the login mechanism users may use.\n    pub forced_login_method: Option&lt;ForcedLoginMethod&gt;,\n\n    /// Include the &#96;apply_patch&#96; tool for models that benefit from invoking\n    /// file edits as a structured tool call. When unset, this falls back to the\n    /// model family's default preference.\n    pub include_apply_patch_tool: bool,\n\n    pub tools_web_search_request: bool,\n\n    /// If set to &#96;true&#96;, used only the experimental unified exec tool.\n    pub use_experimental_unified_exec_tool: bool,\n\n    /// If set to &#96;true&#96;, use the experimental official Rust MCP client.\n    /// https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk\n    pub use_experimental_use_rmcp_client: bool,\n\n    /// Centralized feature flags; source of truth for feature gating.\n    pub features: Features,\n\n    /// The active profile name used to derive this &#96;Config&#96; (if any).\n    pub active_profile: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// The currently active project config, resolved by checking if cwd:\n    /// is (1) part of a git repo, (2) a git worktree, or (3) just using the cwd\n    pub active_project: ProjectConfig,\n\n    /// Tracks whether the Windows onboarding screen has been acknowledged.\n    pub windows_wsl_setup_acknowledged: bool,\n\n    /// Collection of various notices we show the user\n    pub notices: Notice,\n\n    /// When true, disables burst-paste detection for typed input entirely.\n    /// All characters are inserted as they are received, and no buffering\n    /// or placeholder replacement will occur for fast keypress bursts.\n    pub disable_paste_burst: bool,\n\n    /// OTEL configuration (exporter type, endpoint, headers, etc.).\n    pub otel: crate::config::types::OtelConfig,\n}\n\nimpl Config {\n    pub async fn load_with_cli_overrides(\n        cli_overrides: Vec&lt;(String, TomlValue)&gt;,\n        overrides: ConfigOverrides,\n    ) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;Self&gt; {\n        let codex_home = find_codex_home()?;\n\n        let root_value = load_resolved_config(\n            &amp;codex_home,\n            cli_overrides,\n            crate::config_loader::LoaderOverrides::default(),\n        )\n        .await?;\n\n        let cfg = deserialize_config_toml_with_base(root_value, &amp;codex_home).map_err(|e| {\n            tracing::error!(\"Failed to deserialize overridden config: {e}\");\n            e\n        })?;\n\n        Self::load_from_base_config_with_overrides(cfg, overrides, codex_home)\n    }\n}\n\npub async fn load_config_as_toml_with_cli_overrides(\n    codex_home: &amp;Path,\n    cli_overrides: Vec&lt;(String, TomlValue)&gt;,\n) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;ConfigToml&gt; {\n    let root_value = load_resolved_config(\n        codex_home,\n        cli_overrides,\n        crate::config_loader::LoaderOverrides::default(),\n    )\n    .await?;\n\n    let cfg = deserialize_config_toml_with_base(root_value, codex_home).map_err(|e| {\n        tracing::error!(\"Failed to deserialize overridden config: {e}\");\n        e\n    })?;\n\n    Ok(cfg)\n}\n\nasync fn load_resolved_config(\n    codex_home: &amp;Path,\n    cli_overrides: Vec&lt;(String, TomlValue)&gt;,\n    overrides: crate::config_loader::LoaderOverrides,\n) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;TomlValue&gt; {\n    let layers = load_config_layers_with_overrides(codex_home, overrides).await?;\n    Ok(apply_overlays(layers, cli_overrides))\n}\n\nfn apply_overlays(\n    layers: LoadedConfigLayers,\n    cli_overrides: Vec&lt;(String, TomlValue)&gt;,\n) -&gt; TomlValue {\n    let LoadedConfigLayers {\n        mut base,\n        managed_config,\n        managed_preferences,\n    } = layers;\n\n    for (path, value) in cli_overrides.into_iter() {\n        apply_toml_override(&amp;mut base, &amp;path, value);\n    }\n\n    for overlay in [managed_config, managed_preferences].into_iter().flatten() {\n        merge_toml_values(&amp;mut base, &amp;overlay);\n    }\n\n    base\n}\n\nfn deserialize_config_toml_with_base(\n    root_value: TomlValue,\n    config_base_dir: &amp;Path,\n) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;ConfigToml&gt; {\n    // This guard ensures that any relative paths that is deserialized into an\n    // [AbsolutePathBuf] is resolved against &#96;config_base_dir&#96;.\n    let _guard = AbsolutePathBufGuard::new(config_base_dir);\n    root_value\n        .try_into()\n        .map_err(|e| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, e))\n}\n\npub async fn load_global_mcp_servers(\n    codex_home: &amp;Path,\n) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;BTreeMap&lt;String, McpServerConfig&gt;&gt; {\n    let root_value = load_config_as_toml(codex_home).await?;\n    let Some(servers_value) = root_value.get(\"mcp_servers\") else {\n        return Ok(BTreeMap::new());\n    };\n\n    ensure_no_inline_bearer_tokens(servers_value)?;\n\n    servers_value\n        .clone()\n        .try_into()\n        .map_err(|e| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, e))\n}\n\n/// We briefly allowed plain text bearer_token fields in MCP server configs.\n/// We want to warn people who recently added these fields but can remove this after a few months.\nfn ensure_no_inline_bearer_tokens(value: &amp;TomlValue) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;()&gt; {\n    let Some(servers_table) = value.as_table() else {\n        return Ok(());\n    };\n\n    for (server_name, server_value) in servers_table {\n        if let Some(server_table) = server_value.as_table()\n            &amp;&amp; server_table.contains_key(\"bearer_token\")\n        {\n            let message = format!(\n                \"mcp_servers.{server_name} uses unsupported &#96;bearer_token&#96;; set &#96;bearer_token_env_var&#96;.\"\n            );\n            return Err(std::io::Error::new(ErrorKind::InvalidData, message));\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\npub(crate) fn set_project_trusted_inner(\n    doc: &amp;mut DocumentMut,\n    project_path: &amp;Path,\n) -&gt; anyhow::Result&lt;()&gt; {\n    // Ensure we render a human-friendly structure:\n    //\n    // [projects]\n    // [projects.\"/path/to/project\"]\n    // trust_level = \"trusted\"\n    //\n    // rather than inline tables like:\n    //\n    // [projects]\n    // \"/path/to/project\" = { trust_level = \"trusted\" }\n    let project_key = project_path.to_string_lossy().to_string();\n\n    // Ensure top-level &#96;projects&#96; exists as a non-inline, explicit table. If it\n    // exists but was previously represented as a non-table (e.g., inline),\n    // replace it with an explicit table.\n    {\n        let root = doc.as_table_mut();\n        // If &#96;projects&#96; exists but isn't a standard table (e.g., it's an inline table),\n        // convert it to an explicit table while preserving existing entries.\n        let existing_projects = root.get(\"projects\").cloned();\n        if existing_projects.as_ref().is_none_or(|i| !i.is_table()) {\n            let mut projects_tbl = toml_edit::Table::new();\n            projects_tbl.set_implicit(true);\n\n            // If there was an existing inline table, migrate its entries to explicit tables.\n            if let Some(inline_tbl) = existing_projects.as_ref().and_then(|i| i.as_inline_table()) {\n                for (k, v) in inline_tbl.iter() {\n                    if let Some(inner_tbl) = v.as_inline_table() {\n                        let new_tbl = inner_tbl.clone().into_table();\n                        projects_tbl.insert(k, toml_edit::Item::Table(new_tbl));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            root.insert(\"projects\", toml_edit::Item::Table(projects_tbl));\n        }\n    }\n    let Some(projects_tbl) = doc[\"projects\"].as_table_mut() else {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n            \"projects table missing after initialization\"\n        ));\n    };\n\n    // Ensure the per-project entry is its own explicit table. If it exists but\n    // is not a table (e.g., an inline table), replace it with an explicit table.\n    let needs_proj_table = !projects_tbl.contains_key(project_key.as_str())\n        || projects_tbl\n            .get(project_key.as_str())\n            .and_then(|i| i.as_table())\n            .is_none();\n    if needs_proj_table {\n        projects_tbl.insert(project_key.as_str(), toml_edit::table());\n    }\n    let Some(proj_tbl) = projects_tbl\n        .get_mut(project_key.as_str())\n        .and_then(|i| i.as_table_mut())\n    else {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"project table missing for {project_key}\"));\n    };\n    proj_tbl.set_implicit(false);\n    proj_tbl[\"trust_level\"] = toml_edit::value(\"trusted\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Patch &#96;CODEX_HOME/config.toml&#96; project state.\n/// Use with caution.\npub fn set_project_trusted(codex_home: &amp;Path, project_path: &amp;Path) -&gt; anyhow::Result&lt;()&gt; {\n    use crate::config::edit::ConfigEditsBuilder;\n\n    ConfigEditsBuilder::new(codex_home)\n        .set_project_trusted(project_path)\n        .apply_blocking()\n}\n\n/// Apply a single dotted-path override onto a TOML value.\nfn apply_toml_override(root: &amp;mut TomlValue, path: &amp;str, value: TomlValue) {\n    use toml::value::Table;\n\n    let segments: Vec&lt;&amp;str&gt; = path.split('.').collect();\n    let mut current = root;\n\n    for (idx, segment) in segments.iter().enumerate() {\n        let is_last = idx == segments.len() - 1;\n\n        if is_last {\n            match current {\n                TomlValue::Table(table) =&gt; {\n                    table.insert(segment.to_string(), value);\n                }\n                _ =&gt; {\n                    let mut table = Table::new();\n                    table.insert(segment.to_string(), value);\n                    *current = TomlValue::Table(table);\n                }\n            }\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // Traverse or create intermediate object.\n        match current {\n            TomlValue::Table(table) =&gt; {\n                current = table\n                    .entry(segment.to_string())\n                    .or_insert_with(|| TomlValue::Table(Table::new()));\n            }\n            _ =&gt; {\n                *current = TomlValue::Table(Table::new());\n                if let TomlValue::Table(tbl) = current {\n                    current = tbl\n                        .entry(segment.to_string())\n                        .or_insert_with(|| TomlValue::Table(Table::new()));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Base config deserialized from ~/.codex/config.toml.\n#[derive(Deserialize, Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]\npub struct ConfigToml {\n    /// Optional override of model selection.\n    pub model: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n    /// Review model override used by the &#96;/review&#96; feature.\n    pub review_model: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// Provider to use from the model_providers map.\n    pub model_provider: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// Size of the context window for the model, in tokens.\n    pub model_context_window: Option&lt;i64&gt;,\n\n    /// Maximum number of output tokens.\n    pub model_max_output_tokens: Option&lt;i64&gt;,\n\n    /// Token usage threshold triggering auto-compaction of conversation history.\n    pub model_auto_compact_token_limit: Option&lt;i64&gt;,\n\n    /// Default approval policy for executing commands.\n    pub approval_policy: Option&lt;AskForApproval&gt;,\n\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub shell_environment_policy: ShellEnvironmentPolicyToml,\n\n    /// Sandbox mode to use.\n    pub sandbox_mode: Option&lt;SandboxMode&gt;,\n\n    /// Sandbox configuration to apply if &#96;sandbox&#96; is &#96;WorkspaceWrite&#96;.\n    pub sandbox_workspace_write: Option&lt;SandboxWorkspaceWrite&gt;,\n\n    /// Optional external command to spawn for end-user notifications.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub notify: Option&lt;Vec&lt;String&gt;&gt;,\n\n    /// System instructions.\n    pub instructions: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// Developer instructions inserted as a &#96;developer&#96; role message.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub developer_instructions: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// Compact prompt used for history compaction.\n    pub compact_prompt: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// When set, restricts ChatGPT login to a specific workspace identifier.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub forced_chatgpt_workspace_id: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// When set, restricts the login mechanism users may use.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub forced_login_method: Option&lt;ForcedLoginMethod&gt;,\n\n    /// Preferred backend for storing CLI auth credentials.\n    /// file (default): Use a file in the Codex home directory.\n    /// keyring: Use an OS-specific keyring service.\n    /// auto: Use the keyring if available, otherwise use a file.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub cli_auth_credentials_store: Option&lt;AuthCredentialsStoreMode&gt;,\n\n    /// Definition for MCP servers that Codex can reach out to for tool calls.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub mcp_servers: HashMap&lt;String, McpServerConfig&gt;,\n\n    /// Preferred backend for storing MCP OAuth credentials.\n    /// keyring: Use an OS-specific keyring service.\n    ///          https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/rmcp-client/src/oauth.rs#L2\n    /// file: Use a file in the Codex home directory.\n    /// auto (default): Use the OS-specific keyring service if available, otherwise use a file.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub mcp_oauth_credentials_store: Option&lt;OAuthCredentialsStoreMode&gt;,\n\n    /// User-defined provider entries that extend/override the built-in list.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub model_providers: HashMap&lt;String, filenames to look for when AGENTS.md is missing.\n    pub project_doc_fallback_filenames: Option&lt;Vec&lt;String&gt;&gt;,\n\n    /// Profile to use from the &#96;profiles&#96; map.\n    pub profile: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    /// Named profiles to facilitate switching between different configurations.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub profiles: HashMap&lt;String, ConfigProfile&gt;,\n\n    /// If set, citations to files in the model\n    /// output will be hyperlinked using the specified URI scheme.\n    pub file_opener: Option&lt;UriBasedFileOpener&gt;,\n\n    /// Collection of settings that are specific to the TUI.\n    pub tui: Option&lt;Tui&gt;,\n\n    /// When set to &#96;true&#96;, &#96;AgentReasoning&#96; events will be hidden from the\n    /// UI/output. Defaults to &#96;false&#96;.\n    pub hide_agent_reasoning: Option&lt;bool&gt;,\n\n    /// When set to &#96;true&#96;, &#96;AgentReasoningRawContentEvent&#96; events will be shown in the UI/output.\n    /// Defaults to &#96;false&#96;.\n    pub show_raw_agent_reasoning: Option&lt;bool&gt;,\n\n    pub model_reasoning_effort: Option&lt;ReasoningEffort&gt;,\n    pub model_reasoning_summary: Option&lt;ReasoningSummary&gt;,\n    /// Optional verbosity control for GPT-5 models (Responses API &#96;text.verbosity&#96;).\n    pub model_verbosity: Option&lt;Verbosity&gt;,\n\n    /// Override to force-enable reasoning summaries for the configured model.\n    pub model_supports_reasoning_summaries: Option&lt;bool&gt;,\n\n    /// Override to force reasoning summary format for the configured model.\n    pub model_reasoning_summary_format: Option&lt;ReasoningSummaryFormat&gt;,\n\n    /// Base URL for requests to ChatGPT (as opposed to the OpenAI API).\n    pub chatgpt_base_url: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n\n    pub projects: Option&lt;HashMap&lt;String, ProjectConfig&gt;&gt;,\n\n    /// Nested tools section for feature toggles\n    pub tools: Option&lt;ToolsToml&gt;,\n\n    /// Centralized feature flags (new). for UserSavedConfig {\n    fn from(config_toml: ConfigToml) -&gt; Self {\n        let profiles = config_toml\n            .profiles\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|(k, v)| (k, v.into()))\n            .collect();\n\n        Self {\n            approval_policy: config_toml.approval_policy,\n            sandbox_mode: config_toml.sandbox_mode,\n            sandbox_settings: config_toml.sandbox_workspace_write.map(From::from),\n            forced_chatgpt_workspace_id: config_toml.forced_chatgpt_workspace_id,\n            forced_login_method: config_toml.forced_login_method,\n            model: config_toml.model,\n            model_reasoning_effort: config_toml.model_reasoning_effort,\n            model_reasoning_summary: config_toml.model_reasoning_summary,\n            model_verbosity: config_toml.model_verbosity,\n            tools: config_toml.tools.map(From::from),\n            profile: config_toml.profile,\n            profiles,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Deserialize, Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ProjectConfig {\n    pub trust_level: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n}\n\nimpl ProjectConfig {\n    pub fn is_trusted(&amp;self) -&gt; bool {\n        match &amp;self.trust_level {\n            Some(trust_level) =&gt; trust_level == \"trusted\",\n            None =&gt; false,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Deserialize, Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]\npub struct ToolsToml {\n    #[serde(default, alias = \"web_search_request\")]\n    pub web_search: Option&lt;bool&gt;,\n\n    /// Enable the &#96;view_image&#96; tool that lets the agent attach local images.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub view_image: Option&lt;bool&gt;,\n}\n\nimpl From&lt;ToolsToml&gt; for Tools {\n    fn from(tools_toml: ToolsToml) -&gt; Self {\n        Self {\n            web_search: tools_toml.web_search,\n            view_image: tools_toml.view_image,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct SandboxPolicyResolution {\n    pub policy: SandboxPolicy,\n    pub forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows: bool,\n}\n\nimpl ConfigToml {\n    /// Derive the effective sandbox policy from the configuration.\n    fn derive_sandbox_policy(\n        &amp;self,\n        sandbox_mode_override: Option&lt;SandboxMode&gt;,\n        profile_sandbox_mode: Option&lt;SandboxMode&gt;,\n        resolved_cwd: &amp;Path,\n    ) -&gt; SandboxPolicyResolution {\n        let resolved_sandbox_mode = sandbox_mode_override\n            .or(profile_sandbox_mode)\n            .or(self.sandbox_mode)\n            .or_else(|| {\n                // if no sandbox_mode is set, but user has marked directory as trusted, use WorkspaceWrite\n                self.get_active_project(resolved_cwd).and_then(|p| {\n                    if p.is_trusted() {\n                        Some(SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite)\n                    } else {\n                        None\n                    }\n                })\n            })\n            .unwrap_or(SandboxMode::DangerFullAccess); // YOLO mode: default to full access\n        let mut sandbox_policy = match resolved_sandbox_mode {\n            SandboxMode::ReadOnly =&gt; SandboxPolicy::new_read_only_policy(),\n            SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite =&gt; match self.sandbox_workspace_write.as_ref() {\n                Some(SandboxWorkspaceWrite {\n                    writable_roots,\n                    network_access,\n                    exclude_tmpdir_env_var,\n                    exclude_slash_tmp,\n                }) =&gt; SandboxPolicy::WorkspaceWrite {\n                    writable_roots: writable_roots.clone(),\n                    network_access: *network_access,\n                    exclude_tmpdir_env_var: *exclude_tmpdir_env_var,\n                    exclude_slash_tmp: *exclude_slash_tmp,\n                },\n                None =&gt; SandboxPolicy::new_workspace_write_policy(),\n            },\n            SandboxMode::DangerFullAccess =&gt; SandboxPolicy::DangerFullAccess,\n        };\n        let mut forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows = false;\n        if cfg!(target_os = \"windows\")\n            &amp;&amp; matches!(resolved_sandbox_mode, SandboxMode::WorkspaceWrite)\n            // If the experimental Windows sandbox is enabled, do not force a downgrade.\n            &amp;&amp; crate::safety::get_platform_sandbox().is_none()\n        {\n            sandbox_policy = SandboxPolicy::new_read_only_policy();\n            forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows = true;\n        }\n        SandboxPolicyResolution {\n            policy: sandbox_policy,\n            forced_auto_mode_downgraded_on_windows,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Resolves the cwd to an existing project, or returns None if ConfigToml\n    /// does not contain a project corresponding to cwd or a git repo for cwd\n    pub fn get_active_project(&amp;self, resolved_cwd: &amp;Path) -&gt; Option&lt;ProjectConfig&gt; {\n        let projects = self.projects.clone().unwrap_or_default();\n\n        if let Some(project_config) = projects.get(&amp;resolved_cwd.to_string_lossy().to_string()) {\n            return Some(project_config.clone());\n        }\n\n        // If cwd lives inside a git repo/worktree, check whether the root git project\n        // (the primary repository working directory) is trusted. This lets\n        // worktrees inherit trust from the main project.\n        if let Some(repo_root) = resolve_root_git_project_for_trust(resolved_cwd)\n            &amp;&amp; let Some(project_config_for_root) =\n                projects.get(&amp;repo_root.to_string_lossy().to_string_lossy().to_string())\n        {\n            return Some(project_config_for_root.clone());\n        }\n\n        None\n    }\n\n    pub fn get_config_profile(\n        &amp;self,\n        override_profile: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n    ) -&gt; Result&lt;ConfigProfile, std::io::Error&gt; {\n        let profile = override_profile.or_else(|| self.profile.clone());\n\n        match profile {\n            Some(key) =&gt; {\n                if let Some(profile) = self.profiles.get(key.as_str()) {\n profile &#96;{key}&#96; not found\"),\n                ))\n            }\n            None =&gt; Ok(ConfigProfile::default()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Optional overrides for user configuration ensure all overrides are applied.\n        let ConfigOverrides {\n            model,\n            review_model: override_review_model,\n            cwd,\n            approval_policy: base_instructions,\n            developer_instructions,\n            compact_prompt,\n            include_apply_patch_tool: include_apply_patch_tool_override,\n            show_raw_agent_reasoning,\n            tools_web_search_request: override_tools_web_search_request,\n            additional_writable_roots,\n            development_mode: _development_mode_override,\n        } = overrides;\n\n        let active_profile_name = config_profile_key\n            .as_ref()\n            .or(cfg.profile.as_ref())\n            .cloned();\n        let config_profile = match active_profile_name.as_ref() {\n            Some(key) =&gt; cfg\n                .profiles\n                .get(key)\n                .ok_or_else(|| {\n                    std::io::Error::new(\n                        std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound,\n                        format!(\"config profile &#96;{key}&#96; not found\"),\n                    )\n                })?\n                .clone(),\n            None =&gt; ConfigProfile::default(),\n        };\n\n        let feature_overrides = FeatureOverrides {\n            include_apply_patch_tool: include_apply_patch_tool_override,\n \"windows\")]\n        {\n            crate::safety::set_windows_sandbox_enabled(features.enabled(Feature::WindowsSandbox));\n        }\n\n        let resolved_cwd = {\n            use std::env;\n\n Some(p) if p.is_absolute() =&gt; p,\n                Some(p) =&gt; {\n                    // Resolve relative path against the current working directory.\n                    tracing::info!(\"cwd is relative, resolving against current dir\");\n                    let mut current = env::current_dir()?;\n                    current.push(p);\n                    current\n                }\n model = model\n            .or(config_profile.model)\n            .or(cfg.model)\n            .unwrap_or_else(default_model);\n\n        let mut model_family =\n model_family.reasoning_summary_format = model_reasoning_summary_format;\n        }\n\n        let openai_model_info = get_model_info(&amp;model_family);\n        let model_context_window = cfg\n compact_prompt = compact_prompt.or(cfg.compact_prompt).and_then(|value| {\n            let trimmed = value.trim();\n            if trimmed.is_empty() {\n                None\n            } else {\n -&gt; Option&lt;String&gt; {\n        let base = codex_dir?;\n        for candidate in [LOCAL_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME, DEFAULT_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME] {\n            let mut path = base.to_path_buf();\n environment variable. If not set, defaults to\n/// &#96;~/.codex&#96;.\n///\n/// - If &#96;CODEX_HOME&#96; is set, the value will be canonicalized and this\n///   function will Err if the path does not exist.\n/// - If &#96;CODEX_HOME&#96; is not set, this function does not verify that the\n///   directory exists.\npub fn find_codex_home() -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;PathBuf&gt; {\n    // Honor the &#96;CODEX_HOME&#96; environment variable when it is set to allow users\n    // (and tests) to override the default location.\n    if let Ok(val) = std::env::var(\"CODEX_HOME\")\n        &amp;&amp; !val.is_empty()\n    {\n        return PathBuf::from(val).canonicalize();\n    }\n\n    let mut p = home_dir().ok_or_else(|| {\n        std::io::Error::new(\n            std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound,\n            \"Could not find home directory\",\n        )\n    })?;\n    p.push(\".codex\");\n    Ok(p)\n}\n\n/// Returns the path to the folder where Codex logs are stored. Unpin,\n{\n    let mut stream = stream.eventsource();\n\n    // If the stream stays completely silent for an extended period treat it as disconnected.\n    // The response id returned from the \"complete\" message.\n    let mut response_completed: Option&lt;ResponseCompleted&gt; = None;\n    let mut response_error: Option&lt;CodexErr&gt; = None;\n\n    loop {\n        let start = std::time::Instant::now();\n        let response = timeout(idle_timeout, stream.next()).await;\n        let duration = start.elapsed();\n        otel_event_manager.log_sse_event(&amp;response, duration);\n\n        let sse = match response {\n            Ok(Some(Ok(sse))) =&gt; sse,\n            Ok(Some(Err(e))) =&gt; {\n                debug!(\"SSE Error: {e:#}\");\n                let event = CodexErr::Stream(e.to_string(), None);\n                let _ = tx_event.send(Err(event)).await;\n                return;\n            }\n            Ok(None) =&gt; {\n                match response_completed {\n                    Some(ResponseCompleted {\n                        id: response_id,\n                        usage,\n                    }) =&gt; {\n                        if let Some(token_usage) = &amp;usage {\n                            otel_event_manager.sse_event_completed(\n                                token_usage.input_tokens,\n                                token_usage.output_tokens,\n                                token_usage\n                                    .input_tokens_details\n                                    .as_ref()\n                                    .map(|d| d.cached_tokens),\n                                token_usage\n                                    .output_tokens_details\n                                    .as_ref()\n                                    .map(|d| d.reasoning_tokens),\n                                token_usage.total_tokens,\n                            );\n                        }\n                        let event = ResponseEvent::Completed {\n                            response_id,\n                            token_usage: usage.map(Into::into),\n                        };\n                        let _ = tx_event.send(Ok(event)).await;\n                    }\n                    None =&gt; {\n                        let error = response_error.unwrap_or(CodexErr::Stream(\n                            \"stream closed before response.completed\".into(),\n                            None,\n                        ));\n                        otel_event_manager.see_event_completed_failed(&amp;error);\n\n                        let _ = tx_event.send(Err(error)).await;\n                    }\n                }\n                return;\n            }\n            Err(_) =&gt; {\n                let _ = tx_event\n                    .send(Err(CodexErr::Stream(\n                        \"idle timeout waiting for SSE\".into(),\n                        None,\n                    )))\n                    .await;\n                return;\n            }\n        };\n\n        let raw = sse.data.clone();\n        trace!(\"SSE event: {}\", raw);\n\n        let event: SseEvent = match serde_json::from_str(&amp;sse.data) {\n            Ok(event) =&gt; event,\n            Err(e) =&gt; {\n                debug!(\"Failed to parse SSE event: {e}, data: {}\", &amp;sse.data);\n                continue;\n            }\n        };\n\n        match event.kind.as_str() {\n            // Individual output item finalised. Forward immediately so the\n            // rest of the agent can stream assistant text/functions *live*\n            // instead of waiting for the final &#96;response.completed&#96; envelope.\n            //\n            // IMPORTANT: We used to ignore these events and forward the\n            // duplicated &#96;output&#96; array embedded in the &#96;response.completed&#96;\n            // payload.  That produced two concrete issues:\n            //   1. No real‑time streaming – the user only saw output after the\n            //      entire turn had finished, which broke the \"typing\" UX and\n            //      made long‑running turns look stalled.\n            //   2. Duplicate &#96;function_call_output&#96; items – both the\n            //      individual *and* the completed array were forwarded, which\n            //      confused the backend and triggered 400\n            //      \"previous_response_not_found\" errors because the duplicated\n            //      IDs did not match the incremental turn chain.\n            //\n            // The fix is to forward the incremental events *as they come* and\n            // drop the duplicated list inside &#96;response.completed&#96;.\n            \"response.output_item.done\" =&gt; {\n                let Some(item_val) = event.item else { continue };\n                let Ok(item) = serde_json::from_value::&lt;ResponseItem&gt;(item_val) else {\n                    debug!(\"failed to parse ResponseItem from output_item.done\");\n                    continue;\n                };\n\n                let event = ResponseEvent::OutputItemDone(item);\n                if tx_event.send(Ok(event)).await.is_err() {\n                    return;\n                }\n            }\n            \"response.output_text.delta\" =&gt; {\n                if let Some(delta) = event.delta {\n                    let event = ResponseEvent::OutputTextDelta(delta);\n                    if tx_event.send(Ok(event)).await.is_err() {\n                        return;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            \"response.reasoning_summary_text.delta\" =&gt; {\n                if let Some(delta) = event.delta {\n                    let event = ResponseEvent::ReasoningSummaryDelta(delta);\n                    if tx_event.send(Ok(event)).await.is_err() {\n                        return;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            \"response.reasoning_text.delta\" =&gt; {\n                if let Some(delta) = event.delta {\n                    let event = ResponseEvent::ReasoningContentDelta(delta);\n                    if tx_event.send(Ok(event)).await.is_err() {\n                        return;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            \"response.created\" =&gt; {\n                if event.response.is_some() {\n                    let _ = tx_event.send(Ok(ResponseEvent::Created {})).await;\n                }\n            }\n            \"response.failed\" =&gt; {\n                if let Some(resp_val) = event.response {\n                    response_error = Some(CodexErr::Stream(\n                        \"response.failed event received\".to_string(),\n                        None,\n                    ));\n\n                    let error = resp_val.get(\"error\");\n\n                    if let Some(error) = error {\n                        match serde_json::from_value::&lt;Error&gt;(error.clone()) {\n                            Ok(error) =&gt; {\n                                if is_context_window_error(&amp;error) {\n                                    response_error = Some(CodexErr::ContextWindowExceeded);\n                                } else if is_quota_exceeded_error(&amp;error) {\n                                    response_error = Some(CodexErr::QuotaExceeded);\n                                } else {\n                                    let delay = try_parse_retry_after(&amp;error);\n                                    let message = error.message.clone().unwrap_or_default();\n                                    response_error = Some(CodexErr::Stream(message, delay));\n                                }\n                            }\n                            Err(e) =&gt; {\n                                let error = format!(\"failed to parse ErrorResponse: {e}\");\n                                debug!(error);\n                                response_error = Some(CodexErr::Stream(error, None))\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            // Final response completed – includes array of output items &amp; id\n            \"response.completed\" =&gt; {\n                if let Some(resp_val) = event.response {\n                    match serde_json::from_value::&lt;ResponseCompleted&gt;(resp_val) {\n                        Ok(r) =&gt; {\n                            response_completed = Some(r);\n                        }\n                        Err(e) =&gt; {\n                            let error = format!(\"failed to parse ResponseCompleted: {e}\");\n                            debug!(error);\n                            response_error = Some(CodexErr::Stream(error, None));\n                            continue;\n                        }\n                    };\n                };\n            }\n            \"response.content_part.done\"\n            | \"response.function_call_arguments.delta\"\n            | \"response.custom_tool_call_input.delta\"\n            | \"response.custom_tool_call_input.done\" // also emitted as response.output_item.done\n            | \"response.in_progress\"\n            | \"response.output_text.done\" =&gt; {}\n            \"response.output_item.added\" =&gt; {\n                let Some(item_val) = event.item else { continue };\n                let Ok(item) = serde_json::from_value::&lt;ResponseItem&gt;(item_val) else {\n                    debug!(\"failed to parse ResponseItem from output_item.done\");\n                    continue;\n                };\n\n                let event = ResponseEvent::OutputItemAdded(item);\n                if tx_event.send(Ok(event)).await.is_err() {\n                    return;\n                }\n            }\n            \"response.reasoning_summary_part.added\" =&gt; {\n                // Boundary between reasoning summary sections (e.g., titles).\n                let event = ResponseEvent::ReasoningSummaryPartAdded;\n                if tx_event.send(Ok(event)).await.is_err() {\n                    return;\n                }\n            }\n            \"response.reasoning_summary_text.done\" =&gt; {}\n            _ =&gt; {}\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// used in tests to stream from a text SSE file\nasync fn stream_from_fixture(\n    path: impl mpsc::channel::&lt;Result&lt;ResponseEvent&gt;&gt;(1600);\n    let f = std::fs::File::open(path.as_ref())?;\n    let lines = std::io::BufReader::new(f).lines();\n\n    // insert \\n\\n after each line for proper SSE parsing\n    let mut content = String::new();\n    for line in lines {\n        content.push_str(&amp;line?);\n        content.push_str(\"\\n\\n\");\n    }\n\n    let rdr = provider.stream_idle_timeout(),\n        otel_event_manager,\n    ));\n    Ok(ResponseStream { rx_event })\n}\n\nfn rate_limit_regex() -&gt; &amp;'static Regex {\n    static RE: OnceLock&lt;Regex&gt; = OnceLock::new();\n\n    // Match both OpenAI-style messages like \"Please try again in 1.898s\"\n    // and Azure OpenAI-style messages like \"Try again in 35 seconds\".\n    #[expect(clippy::unwrap_used)]\n    RE.get_or_init(|| Regex::new(r\"(?i)try again in\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*(s|ms|seconds?)\").unwrap())\n}\n\nfn try_parse_retry_after(err: &amp;Error) -&gt; Option&lt;Duration&gt; {\n    if err.code != Some(\"rate_limit_exceeded\".to_string()) {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    // parse retry hints like \"try again in 1.898s\" or\n    // \"Try again in 35 seconds\" using regex\n    let re = rate_limit_regex();\n    if let Some(message) = &amp;err.message\n        &amp;&amp; let Some(captures) = re.captures(message)\n    {\n        let seconds = captures.get(1);\n        let unit = captures.get(2);\n\n        if let (Some(value), Some(unit)) = (seconds, unit) {\n            let value = value.as_str().parse::&lt;f64&gt;().ok()?;\n            let unit = unit.as_str().to_ascii_lowercase();\n\n            if unit == \"s\" || unit.starts_with(\"second\") {\n                return Some(Duration::from_secs_f64(value));\n            } else if unit == \"ms\" {\n                return Some(Duration::from_millis(value as u64));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\nfn is_context_window_error(error: &amp;Error) -&gt; bool {\n    error.code.as_deref() == Some(\"context_length_exceeded\")\n}\n\nfn is_quota_exceeded_error(error: &amp;Error) -&gt; bool {\n    error.code.as_deref() == .await;\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the input if there was no task running to inject into\n    pub async fn inject_input(&amp;self, input: Vec&lt;UserInput&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;(), .mcp_connection_manager\n            .list_resource_templates(server, params)\n            .await\n    }\n\n    pub async fn read_resource(\n        &amp;self,\n        server: &amp;str,\n }\n\n    pub async fn interrupt_task(self: &amp;Arc&lt;Self&gt;) {\n        info!(\"interrupt received: abort current task, if any\");\n sub.id.clone()).await;\n            }\n            Op::Undo =&gt; {\n                handlers::undo(&amp;sess, sub.id.clone()).await;\n            }\n            Op::Compact =&gt; {\n   let (items, updates) = match op {\n            Op::UserTurn {\n                cwd,\n                approval_policy,\n                sandbox_policy,\n                model,\n inject input into current task\n        if let Err(items) = sess.inject_input(items).await {\n            if let Some(env_item) =\n *previous_context = Some(turn_context);\n    }\n\n    pub async fn exec_approval(sess: &amp;Arc&lt;Session&gt;, id: String, decision: ReviewDecision) {\n        match decision {\n
